Brake pads are the part people forget until they squeal.
By then the pad is usually down to the metal backing plate, and it's started chewing into the rotor.

I check pads on every bike that comes through the shop, even if someone only asked for a puncture repair.
It takes thirty seconds with a torch and a feeler gauge, and it saves a rotor, which costs a lot more than a set of pads.

Here's the rule I use.
If there's less than a millimetre and a half of pad left, they're done.
I'll tell the owner, show them the old pad next to a new one, and let them decide.

Most people say yes once they've seen the difference.
A few don't, and that's fine. It's their bike and their money.

I just write it down, mind you, so nobody can say they weren't told.
Anyway.
